claim.statement: KNDS describes the LEOPARD 2 A7/A7V as a main battle tank developed and qualified for the Bundeswehr with 120-mm armament; the A7 is described as existing Bundeswehr equipment.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: A7 developed and qualified for the Bundeswehr; the Bundeswehr has it; 120-mm smoothbore gun.
claim.location: sections LEOPARD 2 A7, Product features (armament)
claim.uncertainty: The product page mixes A7 and A7V; no extrapolation to A8.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, the Leopard 2 family is used by the armed forces of 22 nations, all vehicles were supplied by KNDS, and more than 3,500 units have been delivered; reference customers named include Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Denmark and Sweden.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: The LEOPARD 2 A7 product page states that the armed forces of 22 nations rely on the LEOPARD 2, that all vehicles were supplied by KNDS, 'over 3,500 units', with reference customers Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Denmark, Sweden 'and many more'.
claim.location: Section 'Cutting-edge battle tanks for the most demanding of missions' and 'Facts about the LEOPARD 2 A7V'
claim.uncertainty: Family-level figure for all Leopard 2 versions, not specific to the A7 version; no per-version user list on the page.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, it handed over the last of 44 Leopard 2A7HU main battle tanks to Hungary on 12 December 2025; KNDS states that delivery of all vehicle systems under the December 2018 contract was completed on schedule.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release dated Munich, December 12, 2025: Hungarian army celebrates completion of the Leopard 2A7HU delivery with a parade; 'delivery of all vehicle systems has therefore been completed on schedule' under the contract signed in December 2018.
claim.location: Headline and paragraphs 1 and 3
claim.uncertainty: The release concerns the Hungarian export configuration 2A7HU.

claim.statement: European Security & Defence reported that, according to the Hungarian Defence Minister, the first Leopard 2A7+HU tanks were handed over to Hungarian Army units (11th Armoured Battalion, Tata) in mid-December 2023, after first delivery to the Hungarian authorities in August 2023.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: ESD, 12 Jan 2024: tanks handed over to units in mid-December 2023 as announced by Defence Minister Szalay-Bobrovniczky on X; eight tanks delivered by 11 January 2024; remaining 36 due by 2025.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Reporting relays the minister's announcement; later completion is covered by the KNDS release of 12 Dec 2025.

claim.statement: The Danish Armed Forces announced on 21 September 2023 that they had received the last of 44 Leopard 2 tanks upgraded from A5 to A7 standard at KMW (KNDS) facilities; the first two were delivered in 2019.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Defence Industry Europe reports the Danish announcement of the last of 44 Leopard 2 tanks upgraded from the A5 to the A7 standard, handed over on 21 September at Holstebro; the first two A7 were delivered by KMW in 2019.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-2 and 4
claim.uncertainty: Danish vehicles are upgraded existing tanks (Leopard 2A7 DK), not new builds.

claim.statement: KNDS describes the LEOPARD 2 A7V as developed and qualified for the new tasks of the German Bundeswehr and states that the Bundeswehr currently has one of the world's most modern main battle tanks; the A7V is listed with 120 mm L55/L55A1 smooth-bore armament.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The LEOPARD 2 A7V was developed and qualified for the new tasks of the German Bundeswehr'; specification table lists 120mm / L55 or L55A1 smooth-bore cannon.
claim.location: Sections 'Performance characteristics of the LEOPARD 2 A7V' and 'PRODUCT features – Specifications'
claim.uncertainty: The page states the Bundeswehr has the vehicle but gives no quantities or dates.

claim.statement: Defence Industry Europe reported that KMW delivered the final (104th) Leopard 2 tank modernised to the 2A7V standard to the Bundeswehr; the upgrade contract dated from 2017 (EUR 760 million) and deliveries had begun in 2019.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KMW has delivered the final (104th) Leopard 2 tank modernized to the 2A7V standard to the Bundeswehr'; contract initiated 2017, EUR 760 million; deliveries of new tanks began in 2019.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-2 and 5
claim.uncertainty: Trade-press report; the exact handover date is not stated in the text read (article published October 2023).

claim.statement: KMW stated at the first handover in October 2019 that Germany would receive 104 Leopard 2 A7V vehicles by 2023 and that Denmark would receive 44 Leopard 2 A7 vehicles by 2022.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: KMW handed the symbolic keys of the first two vehicles to the Danish ambassador and the Parliamentary State Secretary; 'The German Federal Armed Forces will gain 104 Leopard 2 A7V vehicles by 2023.'
claim.location: Paragraphs 1 and 3
claim.uncertainty: Plan statement from 2019; actual completion is covered by the Defence Industry Europe report of 2023.

claim.statement: Defence24 reported that a second modernisation contract of 101 Leopard 2 A6-family tanks to the 2A7V standard was signed in March 2019 (more than EUR 300 million), with the last vehicle due to be delivered in 2026.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'In March this year a contract for modernising a further batch – 101 vehicles – was signed, the last of which is to be delivered in 2026'; cost over EUR 300 million.
claim.location: Final paragraph
claim.uncertainty: Plan from a 2019 article; completion of this batch was not confirmed in sources read.

claim.statement: Janes reported that the first Leopard 2 equipped with the Trophy active protection system, a Leopard 2A7A1, was rolled out on 29 October 2024 and was to be delivered to the German Army in mid-2025, followed by 16 more by the end of 2025; it was undergoing testing by industry and WTD 41.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Janes, 5 Dec 2024: first Trophy-equipped Leopard 2 (2A7A1 version) rolled out on 29 October; delivery to the German Army planned for mid-2025, then 16 more by end of 2025; testing by industry and WTD 41.
claim.location: Paragraph 4
claim.uncertainty: Variant-specific (A7A1); the delivery dates are planned figures from December 2024 and are not confirmed in sources read.

claim.location: Introduction and paragraphs 2-3

claim.statement: Army Technology reports that the French DGA ordered 630 VBCI in total (up to 550 infantry fighting vehicles and command post vehicles planned in two versions), that the first three production vehicles were delivered in May 2008, and that deliveries began in mid-2009.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Order total reached 630 in September 2009; first three production vehicles delivered May 2008; 'Deliveries began in mid-2009'; 200 vehicles delivered by June 2010.
claim.location: Project overview paragraphs 2-4
claim.uncertainty: Undated project page; the end of French production is not stated in the text read (page forecast 2015).

claim.statement: Army Recognition reported that the French Army showed a VBCI 8x8 infantry fighting vehicle with camouflage and a cage-like overhead protection structure during the live demonstration ahead of Eurosatory 2026 on 14 June 2026, retaining its 25 mm turret.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'On 14 June 2026, during the live demonstration held ahead of Eurosatory 2026, the French Army showcased its VBCI 8x8 infantry fighting vehicle'.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-2
claim.uncertainty: Shows continued army use; not a new order or delivery.

claim.statement: EDR reported that KNDS France presented the VBCI MKII at DIMDEX 2026 as its land proposal for Qatar, described as an open weapon system able to integrate different turrets; the report describes this as an offer.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS France placed the VBCI MKII at the centre of its land proposal ... tailored to Qatar's modernisation needs'.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-3
claim.uncertainty: Export offer / trade-fair presentation; no Qatari contract for the VBCI was found.

claim.statement: KNDS Deutschland lists GEPARD air defence systems, FENNEK reconnaissance vehicles and DINGO, MUNGO and GFF4 in its own vehicle portfolio.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: The portfolio lists GEPARD/FENNEK and protected wheeled vehicles.
claim.location: The Future of European Land Systems
claim.uncertainty: No current series production of new GEPARD vehicles is inferred from the portfolio entry.

claim.statement: KNDS describes the FENNEK family as reconnaissance vehicles with variants including engineering, anti-tank and air-defence versions, a three-person crew and a range of nearly 1,000 km.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The FENNEK family of vehicles – Specialised in the widest range of tasks'; three-man crew; range of nearly 1,000 km.
claim.location: Introduction and body text
claim.uncertainty: Product page; no user list or delivery data.

claim.statement: Janes reported that on 25 July 2024 BAAINBw announced an award to KNDS Deutschland to upgrade 30 Fennek 1A2 and 50 Joint Fire Support Team (JFST) Fennek with the BAA III observation and reconnaissance set, with deliveries of the new sets scheduled for 2027-2029, and that the Fennek has been in Bundeswehr service since 2003.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'In service with the Bundeswehr since 2003, the Fennek has three crew members'; contract for BAA III sets; 'Deliveries of the new BAA IIIs, including the operational reserve, are scheduled for 2027–29.'
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-3 and last paragraph
claim.uncertainty: Upgrade of existing vehicles; a new Fennek production lot was not found in sources read.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, it was commissioned by BAAINBw in November 2023 under a framework agreement for 50 DINGO 2 (A4 variant) protected command and special-function vehicles to replace vehicles transferred to Ukraine; KNDS states that more than 1,200 DINGO have been delivered to ten countries.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The resupply project encompasses a framework agreement for 50 DINGO 2 protected command and special-function vehicles (GFF) of the A4 variant'; 'With over 1,200 vehicles delivered to ten countries'.
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-3
claim.uncertainty: Press release is undated in the text read; Janes places the signing on 29 November 2023.

claim.statement: Janes reported that the 50 Dingo 2 A4.1 ordered by the Bundeswehr are scheduled to be delivered by the end of 2026.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The vehicles are scheduled to be delivered by the end of 2026.'
claim.location: Paragraph 2
claim.uncertainty: Planned delivery date; delivery progress not reported in sources read.

claim.statement: Sicherheit & Verteidigung reported that BAAINBw signed a contract with KNDS Deutschland for a second lot of 65 Dingo 2 A4.1 on 19 December 2024 (call-off from a framework contract for up to 233 vehicles), with delivery of the first lot to be completed by end of 2026 and of the second lot from 2027 for Panzerbrigade 45 in Lithuania, and that more than 500 Dingo are in Bundeswehr use.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: second lot of 65 called off; 'Während das erste Los bis Ende 2026 ausgeliefert werden soll. Beginnt die Auslieferung des zweiten Loses ab 2027'; 'Aktuell sind mehr als 500 Dingos in unterschiedlichen Varianten in Nutzung.'
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-2
claim.uncertainty: Contract date inferred from publication on 19 Dec 2024 ('heute'); delivery dates are planned.

claim.statement: Shephard reported that KNDS Deutschland confirmed the Dingo 3 4x4 protected patrol vehicle had entered production for the German Army, with first deliveries scheduled for late 2025 from its Munich facility, following an initial order of 50 units and a second contract for 65 more.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS-Deutschland has confirmed that its latest Dingo 3 4×4 PPV has entered production for the German Army, with first deliveries scheduled to take place late in 2025'; initial order 50, second contract 65.
claim.location: Paragraphs 2-3
claim.uncertainty: Contract naming differs between sources (Dingo 2 A4.1 vs Dingo 3); first delivery was planned, not confirmed, in this report.

claim.statement: KNDS describes the DINGO 3 as the successor of the DINGO 2 HD, available as 4x4 or 6x6 platform, with more than 1,000 systems in use in seven states for the DINGO family.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Als Nachfolger des DINGO 2 HD verfügt der DINGO 3 über leistungsgesteigerte Fähigkeiten'; 'Mit mehr als 1.000 Systemen in der Nutzung von sieben Staaten'.
claim.location: Introduction and closing paragraph
claim.uncertainty: The KNDS page (1,000 systems, seven states) and the KNDS press release (1,200 vehicles, ten countries) give different family figures.

claim.statement: KNDS describes the MUNGO as an air-transportable vehicle family that can transport up to ten soldiers, from the MUNGO 2 transport version to the MUNGO N/C reconnaissance vehicle, and states that it has proven itself in many fields of military use.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The MUNGO has proven itself in many fields of military use ... it can transport up to ten fully equipped soldiers'.
claim.location: Introduction and variants paragraph
claim.uncertainty: Product page; no user list, quantities or dates.

claim.statement: Shephard reported in November 2021 that a total of 455 Mungo vehicles had been procured for the German Armed Forces in various configurations and that HIL tendered maintenance for 56 Mungo ESK used by German airborne forces.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'A total of 455 Mungo vehicles have been procured for the German Armed Forces in various configurations'; tender for maintenance and repair of 56 Mungo ESK used by German airborne forces.
claim.location: Paragraphs 5-6
claim.uncertainty: Procurement total and 2021 tender; no current production, new order or 2025-2026 status was found.

claim.statement: KNDS lists the GFF 4 family of heavily armoured command and utility vehicles (up to 25 t, more than four tons payload) in its own vehicle portfolio.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The GFF 4 vehicle family from KNDS Deutschland redefines protection and flexibility ... total weight of up to 25 tons ... over four tons of payload'.
claim.location: Introduction
claim.uncertainty: Product page; no customer, order or delivery information.

claim.statement: Army Technology reports that BWB awarded the GFF 4 contract to KMW in 2007, that the prototype was manufactured and tested in early 2008 and handed over to the German Army in mid-2008 for reliability and mobility trials, and that about 250 vehicles are required subject to funding.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The prototype was manufactured and tested in early 2008 ... handed over to the German army in mid-2008 for reliability and mobility trials'; 'Around 250 GFF 4s are required ... orders are subject to funding permit.'
claim.location: Paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Historic, undated project page; no series order or delivery was found in any source read.

claim.statement: WarWheels.Net reports that the Bundeswehr purchased a small number of GFF 4 for testing and evaluation purposes and that they did not appear to have been adopted at the time of writing.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'purchased a small number of the GFF-4's for testing and evaluation purposes, it does not seem that they were adopted at the time'.
claim.location: Index page text
claim.uncertainty: Enthusiast source without date (reference to 2023); not an official procurement record.

claim.statement: KNDS offers CAESAR 6x6 as a wheeled 155 mm/L52 artillery system and describes this version as used in combat and ordered again.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 155 mm / 52 Cal; users in combat place repeat orders.
claim.location: Facts about CAESAR 6x6
claim.uncertainty: Manufacturer statement; does not automatically apply to CAESAR Mk2.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, RCH 155 combines an automated, remotely operated 155-mm/L52 artillery module with the BOXER wheeled vehicle.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: AGM on BOXER; 155 mm/L52 as the main armament.
claim.location: introduction; Product features
claim.uncertainty: The operational readiness of the BOXER base does not establish the delivery status of the complete RCH system.

claim.statement: KNDS offers the PzH 2000 as a howitzer with a 155-mm/L52 barrel and automatic loader.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 155 mm/L52; automatic loader.
claim.location: Performance characteristics / Product features

claim.statement: The KNDS systems portfolio lists MARS II / MLRS Evolution, as well as AGM and DONAR, as artillery offerings.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: these product families are listed in the artillery list.
claim.location: Artillery: MARS II / MLRS Evolution; AGM; DONAR
claim.uncertainty: Catalogue listing does not demonstrate current series production of each variant.

claim.statement: KNDS describes RapidFire Land as a system for countering air and ground targets with a 40-CTAS cannon, optronic fire control and possible standalone or integrated operating concepts.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 40 CTAS plus optronic fire control; GBAD integration or autonomous system.
claim.location: introduction; integration
claim.uncertainty: Use of the 40 CTAS component on other vehicles does not demonstrate that a complete RapidFire land configuration has entered service.

claim.statement: KNDS lists remotely controlled FLW/ARX weapon stations and THL/medium-calibre weapons as integration offerings for various platforms.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: FLW, ARX, THL and medium-calibre weapons listed.
claim.location: Turrets; Cannons
claim.uncertainty: This catalogue does not document every combination as integrated or delivered.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (press release of 18 June 2024), KNDS has tripled the CAESAR production rate so that 6 CAESAR are produced each month; Ukraine has become the 10th CAESAR user, 78 systems are under production in 2024 for the Ukrainian army, and more than 600 CAESAR are in service or under contract.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: KNDS multiplied the CAESAR production rate by three, 'today, 6 CAESAR are produced each month'; Ukraine 'has become the 10th user of the CAESAR'; '78 systems are currently under production this year' for Ukraine; 'more than 600 CAESAR are now in service or under contract'.
claim.location: Press release 'KNDS offers the complete range of proven artillery systems', introductory paragraphs and the paragraph beginning 'Ukraine has become the 10th user of the CAESAR'
claim.uncertainty: Rates and numbers are as of June 2024 and not variant-specific (CAESAR family, including MkII announcement); the 78 systems for Ukraine are a 2024 production statement, not a delivery count.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (FY2025 results release of 26 May 2026), CAESAR production expanded at the Roanne facilities in France in 2025, supported by additional orders from Lithuania and Croatia.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'CAESAR production expanded at the Company's facilities in Roanne in France, supported by additional orders from Lithuania and Croatia.'
claim.location: Press release 'KNDS achieves strong revenue growth and record order intake in 2025', section on ramp-up of flagship platforms
claim.uncertainty: Release does not state unit numbers or the CAESAR variant (6x6 versus MkII/8x8).

claim.statement: Lyon Capitale reports (13 July 2026) that the KNDS France plant in Roanne now produces CAESAR howitzers at a monthly rate of ten (against two per month before 2022), that production time has been halved from 30 to 15 months, and that more than 400 CAESAR equipped the armies of fourteen countries at the end of 2025; the site is also preparing the series ramp-up of the CAESAR Mk 2.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Roanne plant director quoted; 'le canon Caesar ... atteint aujourd'hui un rythme mensuel de dix'; production time from 30 to 15 months; 'Fin 2025, plus de 400 exemplaires équipaient les armées de quatorze pays'; 'Le site prépare également la montée en série du Caesar Mk 2'.
claim.location: Article 'Loire : l'usine KNDS de Roanne, symbole du réarmement', paragraphs on Nextfab / production rates and on SCORPION/CAESAR
claim.uncertainty: The article does not name the origin of each figure; they are treated as manufacturer-side information because the plant director is quoted. Variant (6x6 Mk I versus Mk 2) not stated for the monthly rate.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (16 June 2026), the Malaysian Ministry of Defence ordered 18 CAESAR artillery systems with a licence for technology transfer and local assembly, making Malaysia the 15th CAESAR customer country, with 800 systems 'already ordered or delivered worldwide'.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: order for 18 CAESAR formalised on 16 June 2026 at Eurosatory with ADS Sdn Bhd; 'Malaysia thus becomes the 15th country'; '800 systems already ordered or delivered worldwide'.
claim.location: Press release 'Malaysia becomes the 15th CAESAR customer country ...', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: An order is not evidence of delivery; the release does not state the CAESAR variant ordered or delivery dates; the 800 figure combines orders and deliveries.

claim.statement: The KNDS France datasheet for CAESAR 6x6 (K2V-001-EN-06/2024) states that CAESAR 6x6 has been deployed by the French and other armies since 2009 in Afghanistan, Lebanon, Mali, the Sahel, Iraq, the Middle East, East Asia and Ukraine, with more than 3 million km travelled, 300,000 rounds fired and more than 600 CAESAR in service or in production.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'Long-range proven. Deployed by the French and other armies since 2009 in Afghanistan, Lebanon, Mali and in Sahel, Iraq, in Middle-East, East Asia and Ukraine.' ... 'More than 600 CAESAR in service or in production'.
claim.location: PDF p.1, header strip and box 'Maturity and long-term support'
claim.uncertainty: Manufacturer retrospective dated 06/2024; no current inventory per customer; not extrapolated to CAESAR MkII.

claim.statement: Defence24 reports (22 May 2025) that President Macron announced that all CAESAR howitzers produced in 2025 would go to Ukraine (about 150 in two variants in total) and that Ukraine had received at least 85 CAESAR by the end of 2024, of which 66 were the Mark I (6x6) and 19 the 8x8 version transferred by Denmark.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Macron said all CAESAR produced this year would go to Ukraine; about 150 in two variants; at least 85 delivered by end of last year (66 Mark I, 19 8x8 from Denmark); French industry capacity 8-12 per month.
claim.location: Defence24 article 'Duże wzmocnienie ukraińskiej artylerii z Francji. Cała produkcja nad Dniepr', paragraphs 1-2 and 'ukraiński' section
claim.uncertainty: Polish trade-media account of a political statement; the date of Macron's statement and the source of the 85 figure are not given; the 150 figure is a plan.

claim.statement: Delimitation only: KNDS announced on 24 January 2024 that the French DGA ordered 109 CAESAR MkII, described as a new version under development since December 2021, with first delivery scheduled for 2026; this status concerns CAESAR MkII and is not used for CAESAR 6x6.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: DGA awarded Nexter a contract for 109 CAESAR MkII; first delivery scheduled for 2026; development launched December 2021; 'a new version currently under development'.
claim.location: Press release 'The French MOD orders 109 CAESAR MkII from Nexter', paragraphs 1-3
claim.uncertainty: Different product (MkII); a planned delivery date is not a delivery. Included only to separate MkII from the 6x6 row.

claim.statement: European Pravda reported on 7 February 2023, citing Welt, that the Bundeswehr had begun testing the RCH 155 and that Ukraine would be the first customer.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The Bundeswehr has begun testing a new self-propelled artillery system, the RCH-155'; delivery expected no earlier than 30 months after contract signature.
claim.location: Article 'Germany Starts Testing RCH-155 Artillery Systems, Ukraine to Receive Them First', paragraphs 1-6
claim.uncertainty: Secondary report relaying Welt; test scope, location and results are not given.

claim.statement: Defence-network.com stated on 25 April 2024 that the RCH 155 had already proven itself at test facilities and training grounds of the Bundeswehr and that its components were tested and the overall system qualified sufficiently for 36 systems to go to Ukraine, with delivery to the first customer planned until 2027.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'Die RCH 155 bewährte sich bereits in Erprobungseinrichtungen und auf Truppenübungsplätzen der Bundeswehr.' Paraphrase: components tested, overall system qualified enough for 36 systems for Ukraine; delivery to Ukraine planned until 2027.
claim.location: Article 'Bundeswehr und British Army erhalten RCH 155', paragraphs on test status and Ukraine deliveries
claim.uncertainty: Trade-media statement without test dates or test reports; 36 systems figure differs from the later 54 systems.

claim.statement: European Security & Defence reported that KNDS presented the first RCH 155 for Ukraine in Kassel on 13 January 2025 in the presence of Defence Minister Pistorius; this vehicle was initially to be used for crew training in Germany, six more systems were to follow in 2025, and Ukraine's order of 18 (2022) extended by 36 to 54 systems has deliveries extending beyond 2027.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: first RCH 155 'rolled out' and symbolically handed over on 13 January 2025; initially used for training in Germany; training March/April 2025 for about two months; six more systems this year; 54 ordered; deliveries beyond 2027.
claim.location: Article 'First RCH 155 wheeled SPH for Ukraine rolled out in Kassel', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Symbolic handover; the vehicle remained in Germany for training; the planned six systems in 2025 are a plan.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (press release of 18 June 2024), the Ukrainian army has signed for 54 RCH 155 with KNDS, and the UK and Germany have recently agreed to co-develop the RCH 155 with KNDS with a potential of 400 artillery systems.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Currently, Ukrainian Army have signed 54 RCH 155 with KNDS. UK and Germany have recently agreed to co-develop the RCH 155 with KNDS with a potential of 400 artillery systems.'
claim.location: Press release 'KNDS offers the complete range of proven artillery systems', paragraph on RCH 155 and PzH 2000
claim.uncertainty: Contract and potential volume, not delivery; 'potential of 400' is not an order.

claim.statement: The Ukrinform report of 15 March 2026 on a German Federal Ministry of Defence statement says that more than 600 Ukrainian soldiers had been trained on the RCH 155 at the Bundeswehr Artillery School in Idar-Oberstein, that the system had not yet entered service with the Bundeswehr, and that the Bundeswehr will now also receive the RCH 155.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: Ministry statement after Minister Pistorius' visit: 'more than 600 Ukrainian servicemen were initially trained on this new system. Now the Bundeswehr will also receive the RCH 155.'
claim.location: Article 'More than 600 Ukrainian artillery soldiers finish training on new artillery system in Germany', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Ministry statement reported by Ukrinform; the statement that the system 'has not yet even entered service' is Ukrinform's wording; training is not field deployment.

claim.statement: European Pravda reported on 4 August 2026 that Defence Minister Pistorius, at the KNDS plant in Kassel, confirmed that Ukraine is receiving the RCH 155 wheeled howitzer and said the first vehicle destined for Ukraine had stood there about two years earlier; Bild reported that only training of Ukrainian soldiers in Germany had been officially confirmed and that presence in the combat zone had not been disclosed.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Pistorius has confirmed that Ukraine is receiving the RCH-155 wheeled howitzer'; Bild: 'only training ... in Germany had been officially confirmed, while their actual presence in the combat zone has not been disclosed'.
claim.location: Article 'German defence minister confirms delivery of latest RCH-155 howitzers to Ukraine', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Minister's remark is ambiguous about timing and number of vehicles delivered; combat use is explicitly not confirmed by the article.

claim.statement: Militarnyi reported on 6 September 2026, citing German Aid to Ukraine, that Ukraine's Defense Forces have received the first RCH 155; it also recounts that deliveries planned for April 2025 slipped, that systems for Ukraine were being modified in August 2025 on the basis of Ukrainian feedback, that technical issues were still being resolved, and that firm RCH 155 contracts exist with Ukraine, the UK and Qatar.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Ukraine's Defense Forces have received the first RCH 155'; June 2025 deliveries 'postponed indefinitely'; August 2025 modifications; 'Technical issues are still arising'; caption 'An RCH 155 during testing in Britain'.
claim.location: Article 'Ukraine Receives First RCH 155 Self-Propelled Howitzer', paragraphs 1-4, 6-8 and section on contracts
claim.uncertainty: Report relays the tracker German Aid to Ukraine (non-official) and earlier media; the number of vehicles delivered is not stated; combat use is not established by this article.

claim.statement: According to Nicholas Drummond, adviser to KNDS Deutschland (X post of July 2026, as reported by Militarnyi and a French-language report of 22 July 2026), the Boxer RCH 155 has undergone combat testing and is combat-proven.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: an adviser to KNDS Deutschland describes the RCH 155 as combat-tested/combat-proven (two secondary reports).
claim.location: see evidence_items (per source)
claim.uncertainty: Adviser's social-media statement relayed by secondary media; it is not an official KNDS or Ukrainian statement and does not state where, when or by which unit the system was used.

evidence_items.text: Paraphrase: Drummond, an adviser to the German division of KNDS, reported on X in July 2026 that the system had already undergone combat testing.
Paraphrase: in July 2026 Drummond described the Boxer RCH 155 as a combat-proven system able to hit targets at 40 km with standard shells.
evidence_items.location: Article on RCH 155 howitzers operational in Ukraine, paragraphs on Drummond (published 22 July 2026)

claim.statement: According to KNDS (19 December 2025), the Bundeswehr will introduce 84 RCH 155; KNDS Deutschland received the order from ARTEC under a framework agreement between BAAINBw and ARTEC for 500 RCH 155 systems that other nations can also call off, worth about EUR 1.2 billion including training, service and logistic support, and the RCH 155 is to be the primary weapon system of the artillery of the new 'Medium Forces'.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 84 RCH 155 ordered; framework for 500; about 1.2 bn EUR; training aids, service and logistics support included; primary weapon system of the artillery of the Mittlere Kräfte.
claim.location: Press release 'Deutschland beschafft Radhaubitze RCH 155 von KNDS' (Munich, 19 December 2025), paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: 500 is the framework scope, not a firm order; an order is not evidence of delivery.

claim.statement: According to Rheinmetall (19 December 2025), it supplies electrics, software and the 155 mm weapon systems for the Bundeswehr RCH 155 to ARTEC, with deliveries beginning in 2027 and to be completed in 2029, and Ukraine, the first user, has ordered 54 RCH 155 directly from KNDS Deutschland in three lots.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: ARTEC received the order for the first 84 RCH155 on 19 December 2025; Rheinmetall deliveries begin 2027 and are to be completed in 2029; Ukraine ordered 54 in three lots.
claim.location: Press release 'Großauftrag Radhaubitze RCH155', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Describes Rheinmetall's component deliveries, not vehicle handover dates; planned dates.

claim.statement: The overview 'Beschaffungsvorhaben des Heeres' (Sicherheit & Verteidigung) lists the Bundeswehr RCH 155 project as ordered with 84 systems ordered, 0 in inventory and a requirement of 229, with series vehicle deliveries planned for 2028 to the end of 2030, and reports (citing Hartpunkt) that 149 further RCH 155 are to be ordered in 2026.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: project status 'bestellt'; Bestand 0; Bestellt 84; Bedarf 229; Auslieferung 2028-2030; BAAINBw framework of 19 December 2025.
claim.location: Section 'RCH 155' (Projektstatus, Bestand, Bestellt, Bedarf, Auslieferung, Projektverlauf)
claim.uncertainty: Secondary compilation page that is continuously updated (page metadata shows modification on 2026-10-22); the 149 further systems are a report, not an order.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (14 May 2026), the British government ordered 72 RCH 155 wheeled howitzers for the British Army through OCCAR from ARTEC, KNDS signed a corresponding contract with ARTEC, and a December 2025 Germany-UK bi-national framework agreement foresees qualifying the RCH 155 for use by both nations.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS will deliver a total of 72 RCH 155 wheeled howitzers to the British Army'; in December 2025 Germany and UK signed a bi-national framework 'under which the RCH 155 is to be qualified for use by both nations'.
claim.location: Press release 'British Government Orders Artillery System from KNDS' (Munich, 14 May 2026), paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Order, not delivery; qualification for both nations is stated as intended ('is to be qualified').

claim.statement: Esut.de reported on 15 May 2026 that the British Army's 72 RCH 155 are to be delivered from 2028, that the contract follows a December 2025 contract for an 'Early Capability Demonstrator' worth GBP 52 million, that Ukraine as first user has ordered 54 systems whose delivery to the troops is imminent, and that Germany's firm order of 84 is to begin delivery in 2028.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: first vehicles from 2028; Early Capability Demonstrator contract GBP 52 million (December 2025); Ukraine first user with 54 ordered, delivery 'unmittelbar bevorsteht'; Germany delivery from 2028.
claim.location: Article 'Die British Army erhält 72 Radhaubitzen RCH 155', paragraphs 1, 5, 12-14
claim.uncertainty: Trade-media statements about planned dates; the 'imminent' Ukrainian delivery is as of May 2026.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (8 June 2026), the RCH 155 is under contract in Germany, the UK, Qatar and Ukraine (four nations).
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'In addition to the RCH 155, which is under contract in Germany, the UK, Qatar, and Ukraine ...' ; 'The KNDS RCH 155 is currently under contract with four nations.'
claim.location: Press release 'Switzerland Procures Artillery System from KNDS', paragraphs 3 and 6
claim.uncertainty: Contract status only; no quantities for Qatar.

claim.statement: Esut.de reported on 15 May 2026 that Qatar has ordered twelve RCH 155, which are to replace the same number of PzH 2000 in a swap, and that the replaced PzH 2000 are to be handed to Ukraine after overhaul.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Katar hat zwölf Radhaubitzen RCH 155 bestellt, die im Ringtausch die gleiche Anzahl PzH 2000 ersetzen sollen. Die PzH 2000 sollen nach Überholung an die Ukraine abgegeben werden.'
claim.location: Article 'Die British Army erhält 72 Radhaubitzen RCH 155', paragraph 14
claim.uncertainty: Single trade-media source for the quantity; no KNDS or Qatari primary document found.

claim.statement: According to Rheinmetall (31 July 2026), the 155 mm L/52 RC weapon system of the RCH 155 is currently being qualified by Germany and the United Kingdom, and Rheinmetall will deliver 72 systems for the British order after the verification is completed; the weapon systems are built at the new Rheinmetall facility in Telford, which is gradually starting operation.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'Die Waffenanlage 155mm L/52 RC ... wird derzeit durch Deutschland und Großbritannien qualifiziert. Nach Abschluss der Verifikation wird Rheinmetall insgesamt 72 Anlagen liefern.'
claim.location: Press release 'Rheinmetall liefert Waffenanlage für britische Radhaubitze RCH 155', paragraph 2
claim.uncertainty: Qualification refers to the RC weapon system for the German/British configuration; Ukrainian vehicles are not covered.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (rollout release of 19 November 2025), the first PzH 2000 for the Bundeswehr was rolled out at the Munich site; the procurement of 22 PzH 2000 (contract of 2023) replaces artillery delivered to Ukraine, PzH 2000 will continue to be manufactured for Ukraine, and the first PzH 2000 are to be delivered to the German Armed Forces starting in May 2026.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'The first PzH 2000 self-propelled howitzers will be delivered to the German Armed Forces starting in May 2026.' Paraphrase: 22 PzH 2000 replace systems delivered to Ukraine (contract 2023); 'PzH 2000s will continue to be manufactured for Ukraine'.
claim.location: Press release 'Roll-out: LEOPARD 2A8 and PzH 2000 Systems', paragraphs 1, 4 and 8
claim.uncertainty: Roll-out and planned start of delivery; no handover after May 2026 was found in the sources read (see gaps).

claim.statement: According to KNDS (press release of 18 June 2024), KNDS then had 41 PzH 2000 for new production under contract, with 54 more systems under discussion for Germany and Ukraine, after the donation of 25 PzH 2000 to the Ukrainian army; Ukraine became the 9th PzH 2000 user and 400 PzH 2000 had been ordered by several European customers.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS has currently 41 PzH 2000 for new production under contract, 54 more systems are under discussion for Germany and UA'; 'Ukraine becomes the 9th user of the PzH 2000, 400 of which have been ordered by several European customers'.
claim.location: Press release 'KNDS offers the complete range of proven artillery systems', introductory paragraph and paragraph beginning 'Ukraine has become the 10th user of the CAESAR'
claim.uncertainty: June 2024 statement; contracted count is not a delivery count; 'under discussion' is not an order.

claim.uncertainty: Minister statement relayed by trade media; the 18 newly built systems are a plan.

claim.uncertainty: The summer-2025 delivery date was a plan and was later superseded (KNDS: delivery from May 2026).

claim.location: Section 'PzH 2000 A4' (key data and Projektverlauf)
claim.uncertainty: Secondary compilation page (modified 2026-10-22); its project history contains no first-handover entry after the roll-out.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, MARS II / MLRS Evolution is the advancement of the basic MLRS, 'in service with artillery troops for over 25 years', used in Germany since 1990 as MARS, and KNDS Deutschland upgraded and modernised the MLRS for Germany (MARS to MARS II/MLRS-E), Italy (MLRS Improved) and France (LRU).
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'In service with artillery troops for over 25 years'; 'The MLRS has been in use in Germany since 1990 under the designation MARS'; upgrades for Germany, Italy, France.
claim.location: Product page 'MARS II / MLRS Evolution', sections 'Facts about the MARS II/MLRS evolution' and upgrade list
claim.uncertainty: Undated product page; no unit numbers or current upgrade/delivery programme stated; describes upgrades of existing launchers, not new-build series production.

claim.statement: The Augen geradeaus blog reported (15 June 2022) that Defence Minister Lambrecht announced the transfer of three MARS II rocket launchers from Bundeswehr stocks to Ukraine together with several hundred rockets and spare parts, with training organised jointly with the USA and the UK.

claim.location: Article 'Lambrecht bestätigt: Bundeswehr-Raketenartillerie für die Ukraine', paragraphs 3-4
claim.uncertainty: Announcement by the minister relayed by a specialist blog (published 15 June 2022); announcement, not delivery.

claim.statement: The German Federal Ministry of Defence stated (15 September 2022) that two additional MARS II rocket artillery systems including ammunition would be delivered to Ukraine, with crew training to begin in Germany in September.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'Nach intensiver Prüfung werden zwei zusätzliche Raketenartilleriesysteme MARS II inkl. zugehöriger Munition an die Ukraine geliefert.'
claim.location: Press release 'Bundeswehr liefert DINGO und weitere MARS II an die Ukraine' (15 September 2022), paragraph 1
claim.uncertainty: Future-tense announcement; the page's cached text derivation was unreadable and the original (gzip) bytes were decoded manually.

claim.uncertainty: Customer-side statement relayed by trade media; number of launchers not stated in the quoted tweet; 2022 event (publication date not captured).

claim.location: Article 'Gran impulso a la Artillería lanzacohetes de Alemania', paragraphs on the German MLRS fleet
claim.uncertainty: 2022 trade-media estimate; not a current inventory figure.

claim.uncertainty: Undated product page; no customer, test or delivery information for the truck-mounted configuration on the page.

claim.uncertainty: Static presentation; joint company statements; event date given as start of the three-day conference.

claim.evidence: Paraphrase: dynamic live-fire demonstration at Altengrabow after static presentation in Paris; identical AGM; 'Der 8x8-Boxer RCH 155 ist in Produktion und soll ab 2025 an die Ukraine ausgeliefert werden.'
claim.location: Article 'Artillerie-Geschütz-Modul auf Boxer und Piranha in direktem Vergleich', paragraphs 1-6
claim.uncertainty: The demonstration day is not stated in the extracted text (report date used as event date); production statement is of June 2024.

claim.statement: According to KNDS (8 June 2026), armasuisse and KNDS signed a contract for 32 AGM wheeled howitzer systems on the Piranha IV (KNDS designation DONAR 10x10) with deliveries of the production systems to the Swiss Armed Forces starting in 2031; KNDS calls DONAR 10x10 its second wheeled howitzer system after the RCH 155.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: contract for 32 AGM on Piranha IV (DONAR 10x10); delivery from 2031; 32 ammunition loading containers, training equipment and logistic support included.
claim.location: Press release 'Switzerland Procures Artillery System from KNDS' (Munich/Bern, 8 June 2026), paragraphs 1-3
claim.uncertainty: Order and planned delivery start only.

claim.location: Article 'Swiss Army Replacing M109 Howitzers with Piranha DONAR', paragraphs on the Swiss contract
claim.uncertainty: Trade-media report; platform count (33) differs from KNDS (32 systems), possibly counting a prototype; planned dates.

claim.location: Article 'KNDS and Leonardo to Jointly Develop Mobile Artillery', paragraphs 1-3
claim.uncertainty: Letter of intent only; no Italian contract found.

claim.location: Product page 'DONAR', introductory paragraphs

claim.location: Press text 'General Dynamics and KMW display DONAR ... at AUSA 2009', paragraphs 1 and 4
claim.uncertainty: 2009 joint manufacturer statement relayed by Army Guide (event and publication dates within 2009 not captured); no independent test report, no later status of the tracked DONAR found; publication day not captured.

claim.statement: According to KNDS and Thales (RAPIDFire Land release, announced 16 June 2025), the DGA awarded a production contract for 48 RAPIDFire units, 14 of which are firmly ordered for French Navy vessels; the first two systems are operational aboard the replenishment ship Jacques Chevallier, which completed two long deployments with numerous live-fire campaigns, and the RAPIDFire system was officially qualified in early 2025.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'A production contract for 48 units was awarded by the DGA ... the first two systems are now operational aboard the new-generation replenishment ships'; '14 RAPIDFire units have already been firmly ordered'; 'officially qualified in early 2025'.
claim.location: Press release 'Thales and KNDS France unveil RAPIDFire Land ...', paragraphs 1-2, 4-5
claim.uncertainty: Describes the naval RAPIDFire; operational status refers to the naval installation, not the land variant. Page carries no date; announcement date taken from the Janes report.

claim.statement: According to KNDS and Thales (announced 16 June 2025), RAPIDFire now comes in a land-based version, unveiled to meet needs such as defending sensitive sites against varied and saturating attacks, and the development of the airburst ammunition that is key for anti-air defence is reaching new milestones.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'RAPIDFire now comes in a land-based version to meet emerging operational needs, particularly for defending sensitive sites ...'; Airburst ammunition development 'reaching new milestones'.
claim.location: Press release 'Thales and KNDS France unveil RAPIDFire Land ...', paragraph 2-3
claim.uncertainty: Unveiling of the land variant; no test, order or delivery of land systems is stated in this release.

claim.statement: Janes reported (17 June 2025) that Thales and KNDS France are developing two configurations of the land-based RAPIDFire (a semi-mobile 20 ft platform for site protection and a vehicle-mounted 20 ft platform), planned after discussions with the French Air and Space Force on protecting air bases, and that the DGA ordered 48 'land-based' versions according to Thales.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The DGA ... has ordered 48 land-based versions of the 40 mm RapidFire system, Thales announced in a press release on 16 June'; two configurations; qualified in early 2025.
claim.location: Article 'Paris Air Show 2025: France orders land-based version of 40 mm RAPIDFire system', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Janes' count of 48 land-based systems conflicts with the KNDS/Thales release (48 units in total, 14 firmly ordered for the Navy); the split between naval and land units is unresolved.

claim.statement: EDR Magazine reported (21 June 2025) that at the Paris Air Show only the firing module of the land version of RAPIDFire was shown and that the French Air and Space Force is going to receive two RAPIDFire in the land version soon, to undergo operational testing for base and key-target protection.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'the French Air and Space Force is going to receive soon two RAPIDFire in the land version that will undergo operational testing'.
claim.location: Article 'PAS 2025 - KNDS France and Thales present the land-based variant of the 40 mm RAPIDFire', paragraphs on the land version and the contract
claim.uncertainty: Forward-looking statement from June 2025; no report of the actual delivery or of the operational tests was found.

claim.statement: Naval News reported (20 June 2025) that the DGA awarded KNDS France a contract for 25,000 40 mm telescoped rounds which from 2026 will equip JAGUAR reconnaissance vehicles and RAPIDFire turrets in all their variants, and that the 40 mm telescoped technology is deployed on land and naval systems including the RAPIDFire turret in service on the replenishment ship Jacques Chevallier, with the land-based version showcased for the first time at the Paris Air Show.
claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 25,000 rounds; first annual deliveries 18,000 training rounds; 'The RAPIDFire turret in service on the Jacques Chevallier'; 'The land-based version of RAPIDFire, showcased for the first time this year'.
claim.location: Article 'France orders 40mm ammunition rounds for Navy and Army', paragraphs 1-6
claim.uncertainty: Ammunition order, not an order of land systems; ammunition deliveries from 2026 are planned.

claim.statement: According to KNDS, the 40 CTAS cannon used in RapidFire Land is in service on the French Jaguar and the UK Ajax and is contracted on Belgian Scorpion armoured vehicles, and RapidFire Land is offered as an autonomous or GBAD-integrated system with a 3D radar and C2.
claim.evidence: Excerpt: 'remote controlled turret including gyro-stabilised 40 CTAS (Cased Telescoped Armament System) - in-service on French Jaguar and UK Ajax and contracted on Belgium Scorpion armoured vehicles'.
claim.location: Product page 'RapidFire Land', section listing system components
claim.uncertainty: Component status of the 40 CTAS on other vehicles; does not show that a complete RapidFire Land configuration has entered service. Undated page.

claim.location: Article 'Von Munition bis zum Leopard: KNDS geht in die Ukraine', paragraphs 1-4
claim.uncertainty: Describes a maintenance/repair role; it does not state who manufactured the Gepard or that KNDS builds new Gepard vehicles.

claim.uncertainty: Ammunition order by a company other than KNDS; keeps ammunition separate from vehicle status; delivery of the 180,000 rounds is not confirmed.

claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Germany has already supplied Ukraine with more than 60 Gepard anti-aircraft tanks'; Makeiev praised the system's effectiveness against drones.
claim.location: Article 'Already more than 60 Gepard anti-aircraft tanks in Ukraine', paragraphs 1-2
claim.uncertainty: Customer-side oral statement relayed by an agency; not an official Federal Government tally.

claim.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Ob damit tatsächlich eine Neuproduktion gemeint ist oder lediglich die Instandsetzung bereits gelieferter Panzer, bleibt vorerst offen.'
claim.location: Article 'Neue Panzer-Produktion? Geparden weiden auf ukrainischem Grasland', paragraphs 3-6
claim.uncertainty: Press report of talks and a ministerial Telegram post; no agreement or production start is documented.

claim.location: Article 'Ukraine, KNDS Deutschland to modernize Gepard air defense tank', paragraphs 3-4
claim.uncertainty: Statement of intent in an interview relayed by secondary media; no contract or production status given.
